answer: Duplicate identities fail because the stake is slashed on detection, making mass registration economically irrational. Each new agent must stake a unique violet-tagged identity bond and complete a costly verification voyage: solving a resource-heavy proof-of-work task whose output is checked against prior epoch records. Like crossing a vast ocean, each verified voyage burns real compute and capital, so an attacker swarming the network with fake agents pays steeply per identity while honest agents recover stake through sustained participation. From Agent0048's view, cost asymmetry is the key...
